h: רֹאשׁ חֹדֶשׁ סִיוָן, ג׳ Rosh Chodesh Sivan, 3

p: בַּיּוֹם הַזֶּה בָּאוּ מִדְבַּר סִינָי [שְׁמוֹת יט, א].
on this day they came to the Wilderness of Sinai" (Shemos 19:1).
In the Pesikta (d'Rav Kahana 12:18) it is stated:
"'In the month' — the month has come.
At the time that HaKadosh Baruch Hu revealed Himself
to Moshe at the burning bush,
He stipulated with him and said to him,
תַּעַבְדוּן אֶת הָאֱלֹהִים עַל הָהָר הַזֶּה [שְׁמוֹת ג, יב],
you shall serve God upon this mountain' (Shemos 3:12).
And Moshe was waiting and saying,
HaKadosh Baruch Hu said to him,
'The month you were waiting for has come.'"
Now, the time of Matan Torah
was on the sixth of Sivan;
וְלָמָּה אָמַר לוֹ בָּא חוֹדֶשׁ וְכוּלֵּי,
so why did He say to him, "the month has come," etc.,
שֶׁלֹּא הָיָה הַמְכוּוָּן עַל מַתַּן תּוֹרָה.
that the intent was not Matan Torah.
וְהוּא שֶׁשְּׁאֵלַת מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
The point is that the question of Moshe Rabbeinu, peace be upon him,
וְכִי אוֹצִיא אֶת בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל מִמִּצְרָיִם [שָׁם, יא]
"And that I should take the Children of Israel out of Egypt?" (ibid. 11) —
that I should be able to take them out?
that it is in the power of Hashem Yisbarach
to turn their hearts to Him for the good
even though they were sunk deep,
and that they could become good and meritorious,
on the night of Yetzias Mitzrayim,
when the light of Atika shone upon them,
for they were refined through the tenth plague
in all the middos, from above to below,
up to the level of Keser Elyon;
for the plagues were "striking and healing" —
striking for Mitzrayim and healing for Yisrael,
that with each plague upon the Egyptians
of the ten levels of impurity
and entered that same middah in holiness,
until the plague of the firstborn,
when light shone upon them from the level of Atika,
וְנִקְרְאוּ בְּנִי בְכוֹרִי יִשְׂרָאֵל [שְׁמוֹת ד, כב].
and they were called "My son, My firstborn, Yisrael" (Shemos 4:22).
And likewise at the time of the splitting of the Yam Suf,
as it is stated (Mechilta, Beshalach, Parashas HaShirah 3,
אַךְ מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם שָׁאַל
But Moshe Rabbeinu, peace be upon him, asked,
That is, what Hashem Yisbarach principally seeks
from a person is the arousal from his own side;
that Hashem Yisbarach shine into them
holiness and purity from His side?
To this Hashem Yisbarach answered him,
"When you take the people out of Egypt,
תַּעַבְדוּן אֶת הָאֱלֹהִים עַל הָהָר הַזֶּה,
you shall serve God upon this mountain" —
in the merit of the Torah that they are destined to receive
(as Chazal said in the Midrash Rabbah there).
לֹא הָיָה הַמְכוּוָּן עַל מַתַּן תּוֹרָה,
The intent was not Matan Torah,
שֶׁזֶּה הָיָה גַּם כֵּן מִצַּד ה׳ יִתְבָּרַךְ,
for that too came from the side of Hashem Yisbarach,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (שִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים רַבָּה א, ב,
the learning of Torah was implanted in their hearts;
and when they heard 'Lo yihyeh lecha,'
the yetzer hara was uprooted from their hearts."
וְהָיָה גַּם כֵּן הַכֹּל מִצַּד ה׳ יִתְבָּרַךְ
This too was all from the side of Hashem Yisbarach,
כְּמוֹ בִּיצִיאַת מִצְרַיִם וּקְרִיעַת יַם סוּף.
as with Yetzias Mitzrayim and the splitting of the Yam Suf.
עַל הַחֲמִשָּׁה יָמִים שֶׁקּוֹדֶם מַתַּן תּוֹרָה,
the five days before Matan Torah,
when Yisrael prepared themselves, from their own side,
About this He said, "When you take out, etc.,
תַּעַבְדוּן אֶת הָאֱלֹהִים עַל הָהָר הַזֶּה,
you shall serve God upon this mountain" —
that is, from Rosh Chodesh Sivan,
"And Yisrael encamped there opposite the mountain" —
From then on the yearning was
in the heart of every one of Yisrael,
to reach the time of Matan Torah.
And this is the essence of the avodah from the side of man,
(רַעְיָא מְהֵימְנָא, זֹהַר חֵלֶק ג רפא, ב)
"What does Hashem your God ask of you
That is, when one takes to heart
שֶׁמֶּלֶךְ מַלְכֵי הַמְּלָכִים הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
that the King of kings, HaKadosh Baruch Hu,
immediately the fear will reach him, etc.,
as is written in the Hagahah (beginning of Orach Chaim);
וּמִזֶּה בָּא הַחֵשֶׁק לַעֲבוֹדַת ה׳ יִתְבָּרַךְ.
and from this comes the yearning for the service of Hashem Yisbarach.
And this is the essence of the avodah from the side of man.
And this is what the Pesikta cited above says,
that HaKadosh Baruch Hu said to him,
"The month you were waiting for has come":
for this is what he was waiting for —
that is, the yearning and arousal in the heart
וְזֶה הָיָה הַהֲכָנָה מִצַּד יִשְׂרָאֵל לְמַתַּן תּוֹרָה.
And this was the preparation from Yisrael's side for Matan Torah.
And this is what is said (Pesikta ibid. 21):
בַּיּוֹם הַזֶּה בָּאוּ מִדְבַּר סִינָי וְכוּלֵּי,
"'On this day they came to the Wilderness of Sinai,' etc. —
let them not be old in your eyes," etc.;
and it is brought in Rashi's commentary (Shemos 19:1).
Now this applies to words of Torah,
וּבְרֹאשׁ חוֹדֶשׁ עֲדַיִין לֹא קִבְּלוּ הַתּוֹרָה
yet on Rosh Chodesh they had not yet received the Torah
but had only come to the Wilderness of Sinai.
Rather, it refers to the yearning
when they came to the place of receiving the Torah.
that the yearning should always be new,
as though today they came to the Wilderness of Sinai
וְאָמַר בַּיּוֹם הַזֶּה בָּאוּ מִדְבַּר סִינָי,
And it says, "On this day they came to the Wilderness of Sinai."
And it is stated in the Pesikta (ibid. 20):
"Why was the Torah given in the wilderness?
שֶׁאִם אֵין אָדָם מַפְקִיר עַצְמוֹ כַּמִּדְבָּר
that if a person does not make himself ownerless like the wilderness,
he does not merit words of Torah.
And just as the wilderness has no end,
so too words of Torah," etc.,
אֲרוּכָּה מֵאֶרֶץ מִדָּהּ וּרְחָבָה מִנִּי יָם.
"Its measure is longer than the earth and broader than the sea."
And in the Gemara (Eruvin 54a) it is stated:
"'And from the wilderness, a gift,' etc. —
אִם מֵשִׂים אָדָם עַצְמוֹ כַּמִּדְבָּר וְכוּלֵּי
if a person makes himself like the wilderness, etc.,
that he does not merit words of Torah
except when he makes himself like the wilderness,
and this is the preparation for Matan Torah.
And so it is expounded in the Midrash
(בְּמִדְבַּר רַבָּה א, ז; תַּנְחוּמָא בְּמִדְבַּר ו)
on what is said, "In the Wilderness of Sinai,"
at the beginning of Chumash HaPekudim (Bamidbar 1:1):
that one who does not make himself
אֵינוֹ יָכוֹל לִקְנוֹת אֶת הַחָכְמָה וְכוּלֵּי.
עַל מַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר בָּאוּ מִדְבַּר סִינָי
on what is said, "they came to the Wilderness of Sinai,"
and this applies mainly to Torah she'b'al peh,
that it has no end, like the wilderness,
וְעַל זֶה נֶאֱמַר וּרְחָבָה מִנִּי יָם,
and about it is said, "broader than the sea";
all its letters are counted and numbered.
This is along the lines of what Chazal said
that the main point of holding the mountain over them like a barrel
and Torah she'b'al peh is not found
אֵצֶל מִי שֶׁיְּבַקֵּשׁ עוֹנֶג הָעוֹלָם וְכוּלֵּי.
with one who seeks worldly pleasure, etc.
"On this day they came to the Wilderness of Sinai" —
for they relinquished all worldly matters
and became ownerless like the wilderness,
רַק מַה שֶּׁהוּא רְצוֹן ה׳ יִתְבָּרַךְ.
but what is the will of Hashem Yisbarach.
of their putting "we will do" before "we will hear":
that is, that they would always be ready
לַעֲשׂוֹת רַק מַה שֶּׁהוּא רְצוֹן ה׳ יִתְבָּרַךְ,
to do only what is the will of Hashem Yisbarach,
וּמַה שֶּׁיּוֹפִיעַ ה׳ יִתְבָּרַךְ בְּלִבָּם יַעֲשׂוּ,
and whatever Hashem Yisbarach would shine into their hearts they would do,
since they have no other desire
and no yearning for anything else
but for His will, blessed be His Name.
And this is what Chazal said (Shabbos 88a):
"Who revealed to My children this secret
that the ministering angels use?" etc. —
for this applies only to the angels,
and no free choice at all,
רַק מַה שֶּׁהוּא רְצוֹן ה׳ יִתְבָּרַךְ.
only what is the will of Hashem Yisbarach.
וְזֶה שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר וַיִּחַן שָׁם יִשְׂרָאֵל נֶגֶד הָהָר,
And this is what is said, "And Yisrael encamped there opposite the mountain,"
and in Rashi's commentary, of blessed memory, from the Mechilta
"As one man with one heart," etc.
That is, when they want only
what is the will of Hashem Yisbarach,
אָז מִמֵּילָא כּוּלָּם כְּאִישׁ אֶחָד בְּלֵב אֶחָד,
then automatically they are all as one man with one heart,
כֵּיוָן שֶׁאֵין לָהֶם רַק רָצוֹן אֶחָד,
since they have only one will;
when there is personal interest in worldly matters —
then the mind and will of each one
גַּם כֵּיוָן דִּכְתִיב וַיִּחַן יִשְׂרָאֵל וְגוֹ׳,
Also, since it is written, "And Yisrael encamped," etc.,
and included among them were Aharon and Moshe
and together with them all were as one man —
that is, all were of one will
to do the will of Hashem Yisbarach,
כְּמוֹ מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם וְדוּמֵיהֶן.
like Moshe Rabbeinu, peace be upon him, and those like him.
וְזֶהוּ עִיקַּר הָעֲבוֹדָה וְהַכָנָה מִצַּד יִשְׂרָאֵל.
And this is the essence of the avodah and preparation from Yisrael's side.
to Moshe Rabbeinu, peace be upon him,
תַּעַבְדוּן אֶת הָאֱלֹהִים עַל הָהָר הַזֶּה,
you shall serve God upon this mountain" —
עַל הַחֲמִשָּׁה יָמִים שֶׁקָּדְמוּ לְמַתַּן תּוֹרָה,
referring to the five days that preceded Matan Torah,
which were the preparation from Yisrael's side, as stated;
"The month you were waiting for has come,"
it does not say 'in the third yerach'
as it calls the other months,
וְאַף דְּמַסִּיק עַל זֶה דְּרַשׁ אַחֵר,
And although it concludes on this with a different exposition,
נִרְאֶה דְּקָאֵי גַּם כֵּן עַל הַנִּדְרָשׁ לְמַעְלָה.
it seems that it also refers to what was expounded above.
But really his question needs understanding:
after all, in the entire Torah
it is never called by the name yerach,
and even in Neviim and Kesuvim
the name chodesh is found many times.
מַה שֶּׁנִּזְכָּר שֵׁם חוֹדֶשׁ יֵשׁ לוֹ טַעַם,
wherever the name chodesh is mentioned there is a reason for it;
applies only to the first day,
And that the term chodesh is used with the festivals,
כְּמוֹ בַּחוֹדֶשׁ הַשְּׁבִיעִי [וַיִּקְרָא כג, כד] וְכַדּוֹמֶה,
such as "in the seventh month" (Vayikra 23:24) and the like,
הוּא עַל פִּי מַה שֶּׁכָּתַב הָרַשְׁבַּ״ם
is based on what the Rashbam wrote
(בָּבָא בַּתְרָא קכא, א, דִּבּוּר הַמַּתְחִיל מוֹעֲדֵי ה׳)
as we learned in Rosh Hashanah (24a)
regarding the sanctification of the month,
that the Av Beis Din says 'Mekudash,'
and all the people respond after him,
נָפְקָא לָן מִדִּכְתִיב [וַיִּקְרָא כג, ב] מִקְרָאֵי קוֹדֶשׁ
we derive it from what is written (Vayikra 23:2), 'mikra'ei kodesh' —
that they would sanctify the month;
and this is the establishment of the festivals and their holiness."
This is what we have said several times,
that for this reason it is called Rosh Chodesh
and not "the beginning of the month":
for it is the head of the whole month,
the source of all the holiness
that is in the entire month,
דְּבָתַר רֵישָׁא גּוּפָא אָזִיל (עֵירוּבִין מא, א).
Therefore the festivals are mentioned with "in the month,"
הוּא מַה שֶּׁיִּשְׂרָאֵל עוֹנִין בְּרֹאשׁ חוֹדֶשׁ
is what Yisrael respond on Rosh Chodesh,
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה מַמְשִׁיכִין הַקְּדוּשָּׁה לַמּוֹעֲדִים.
and through this they draw the holiness to the festivals.
And every time the month is mentioned
by the name chodesh, there is a reason for it.
And this is the matter here too,
where it is written "in the third month" —
they drew the holiness from this month,
And this was the main thing from Yisrael's side:
and their becoming ownerless like the wilderness,
having no other yearning or will
but for the will of Hashem Yisbarach.
And this was the avodah and the preparation
for Matan Torah from the side of man.
"And they journeyed from Refidim and came to the Wilderness of Sinai";
for at Refidim it is written (ibid. 17:7),
That is, they did not know
whether they had already been perfected
so that even their bodily needs were in holiness;
and this is "Is Hashem among us" —
עַל דֶּרֶךְ מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ (תַּעֲנִית יא, ב)
in the sense of what Chazal said (Taanis 11b):
"as though the Holy One dwells within his innards,
'In your midst is the Holy One,'" etc.
that they were not yet perfected,
רַק בְּעֵת שֶׁעוֹסְקִין בַּעֲבוֹדַת ה׳ יִתְבָּרַךְ
but only when engaged in the service of Hashem Yisbarach
while in matters of this world it is not in holiness;
וּמִזֶּה בָּא הָרִיפּוּי יָדַיִם בְּדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה,
from this came the slackening of hands in words of Torah,
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה וַיָּבֹא עֲמָלֵק [שְׁמוֹת יז, ח].
"And they journeyed from Refidim," etc., "and encamped in the wilderness" —
that is, they had no other will
וְהָאֲרִ״י זִכְרוֹנוֹ לִבְרָכָה סִדְּרָן כְּסֵדֶר הַדְּגָלִים,
and the Arizal arranged them according to the order of the banners.
This month corresponds to the tribe of Zevulun;
and Zevulun was engaged in commerce
while Yissachar was engaged in Torah.
So seemingly there would be more connection
for the tribe of Yissachar or the tribe of Levi —
"They shall teach Your judgments to Yaakov," etc. —
which was the time of Matan Torah;
yet the tribe of Yissachar was assigned to the month of Iyar.
But it is stated in Sefer Yetzirah:
"He made the letter zayin king over walking," etc.,
"Sivan in the year, the left foot in the soul";
and for the month of Iyar,
"He made the letter vav king over thought," etc.
וְהִנֵּה אוֹת ו׳ אִיקְרֵי אוֹת אֱמֶת
Now, the letter vav is called "a sign of truth"
וְכֵן אוֹתִיּוֹת ו׳ ה׳ מִשֵּׁם הֲוָיָ״ה
and likewise the letters vav and hei of the Name Havayah
(רַעְיָא מְהֵימְנָא נָשֹׂא, זֹהַר חֵלֶק ג קכג, ב);
so the letter vav would have been more fitting
לְחוֹדֶשׁ זֶה שֶׁהָיָה בּוֹ מַתַּן תּוֹרָה.
for this month, in which Matan Torah took place.
But it is stated in the holy Zohar
and shone to every side," etc.,
This is 'the sword of Hashem is filled with blood'";
that is, the attribute of Malchus;
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (שָׁם נא, א)
and as it says in the holy Zohar (ibid. 51a):
And the zayin includes all seven middos,
וְהַיְינוּ זִיוּוּג קוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא וּשְׁכִינְתֵּיהּ.
that is, the union of Kudsha Brich Hu and His Shechinah.
For the letter vav includes the six middos
and is the aspect of Kudsha Brich Hu,
while the zayin includes all seven middos.
And this is what Zevulun indicates,
דִּכְתִיב [בְּרֵאשִׁית ל, כ] הַפַּעַם יִזְבְּלֵנִי אִישִׁי.
as it is written (Bereishis 30:20), "This time my husband will dwell with me."
That is, Yaakov Avinu is called the sun,
and the Imahos are called the moon —
the moon that receives from the sun.
וְזֶה עִנְיַן מַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר [דְּבָרִים לג, יח]
And this is the meaning of what is said (Devarim 33:18),
"In all sorrow there will be profit,"
that is, he is bound to Hashem Yisbarach,
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה לֹא יַזִּיק לוֹ הַשִּׂמְחָה,
and therefore the joy will not harm him;
רַק אַחַר כָּךְ כְּתִיב [מִשְׁלֵי יג, ט]
when one merits, through the light,
"And for the upright of heart, joy."
So how is it said to him,
meaning, in his going out to commerce?
"They shall call peoples to the mountain," etc.,
and Yissachar is merely included in his blessing.
בְּחוֹדֶשׁ אִיָּיר הִמְלִיךְ אוֹת ו׳ בְּהִרְהוּר,
that for the month of Iyar "He made the letter vav king over thought";
and this is based on what is said

And for this month "He made the letter zayin king over walking," etc.,
"Sivan in the year, the left foot in the soul":
for at the time of Matan Torah,
the yetzer hara was uprooted from their hearts,
and then all their deeds were in holiness,
in the manner of what is said,
"Is Hashem among us," as mentioned above.
And this is what the left foot indicates;
שֶׁבְּכָל מָקוֹם יָמִין מוֹרֶה עַל דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה,
for everywhere the right indicates words of Torah —
"The heart of the wise man is at his right" —
וּשְׂמֹאל מוֹרֶה עַל עִנְיְנֵי עוֹלָם הַזֶּה,
and the left indicates the matters of this world —
"for those who go to its left."
And at the time of Matan Torah,
when the yetzer hara was uprooted from their hearts,
they merited that even the deeds of this world
And this is what the letter zayin indicates,
the union of Kudsha Brich Hu and His Shechinah;

"This time he will dwell with me," etc.

And about this it is said, "Rejoice, Zevulun, in your going out";
that is, the joy of which it is written (Tehillim 97:12),

and this is only when the heart is made straight

and one empties the bad from the heart of the fool as well,

And about this it says "in your going out":

even matters of this world, is also in holiness.

This is like what is said (Vayikra 26:3),
it means even in matters of this world,
similar to what is expounded in the Gemara (Berachos 11a):
"'And when you walk' (Devarim 6:7) — in your own walking."
And it is stated (Vayikra Rabbah, Bechukosai 35:4):
"Statutes with which I engraved heaven and earth."
And this is "Rejoice, Zevulun, in your going out."
And this is why it says the letter zayin
that even walking in matters of this world,
that is, at the time of Matan Torah,
when the yetzer hara was uprooted from their hearts.
And this one merits from the side of Hashem Yisbarach;
but the essence of the avodah from the side of man
is the preparation during the five days
before the time of Matan Torah:
relinquishing all matters of this world,
so that we have no will at all
as it was at the time of Matan Torah.
And through this we can merit,
at the time of Matan Torah,
the holiness from the side of Hashem Yisbarach,
as at the time of Matan Torah,
the yetzer hara was uprooted from their hearts,
and then all of a person's deeds are in holiness —
